- Difficulty breathing or shortness of breath
- Persistent pain or pressure in the chest or abdomen
- Sudden dizziness or confusion

Yes, it is quite normal to experience heartburn after eating spicy food. When the LES is relaxed, stomach acid can flow back into the esophagus, causing a burning sensation in the chest, commonly known as heartburn.

Additionally, spicy foods can irritate the lining of the esophagus, making the burning sensation feel more intense. This reaction varies from person to person — some may be more sensitive to spicy foods than others.

If heartburn occurs frequently or is severe, it may be a sign of gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), and it's a good idea to consult a healthcare professional for further evaluation and management. In the meantime, you can try avoiding spicy foods, eating smaller meals, and avoiding lying down immediately after eating to help reduce symptoms.
